text: Applying to a PhD is a team sport most students play alone.
Offer room gives a student a team, in the chat app she already uses: six AI agents, each a real role, each starting from a different place. They agree, add, or push back with evidence. She decides.
In Discord, each one shows up as that person, and names what it will check first.
It's built with Switch: one template, six Claude Code agents on this laptop, five Discord rooms.
Two applicants. Both fictional, and I type their side.
Priya, in Tamil Nadu, wants AI that understands her grandmother's Tamil. Her family can afford two applications.
Maya, in El Paso, is the first in her family to go to college, with three hundred dollars saved.
Priya asks which two schools. Scout reads only the official pages: Washington and Cornell. Mentor agrees from the papers, but warns that Cornell rests on one advisor.
Critic closes the round: where they agree, where they split, what only she can decide. Then it corrects its own close, before anyone asks.
Maya asks the same team. Scout won't name a school it hasn't checked. Mentor finds the labs closest to her problem, at Carnegie Mellon.
Funder does the math: a fourth application only fits on a waiver. Critic leaves the call to Maya.
Same desk, same question, different lives. Maya can apply everywhere. Priya, on a student visa, has one waiver.
Getting in is only the start. Mentor reads the professor's own page: her one graduate became a professor.
In the interview room, the agent plays a real professor, from her public papers, and says it's practice. It remembers Priya doubted herself before, and tells her to stop.
Then it digs: your data is social media, but your grandmother talks to a phone menu. Priya names the gap. Depth goes up.
At the writing desk, writer asks for the one detail only Maya can give, and critic won't let anyone invent it.
The checker fails any sentence without a source, and any paper no tool returned. No agent sends, submits or pays.
Getting in is the start, not the finish. Offer room. Built with Switch.
